notes: Introduce the focused repeat-meeting use case. This is a working local application, not a production deployment. CRM is synthetic. Public retrieval is verified; a saved and human-reviewed live OpenAI run remains pending.

title: Continuity across scientific conversations
lead: Before the next meeting, the MSL needs prior context, relevant evidence and the unresolved request in one place.
body:
What happened?

  • Prior discussions and observations
  • Outstanding tasks and medical requests
  • An exact, dated KOL record

What supports it?

  • Literature and registered studies
  • Explicit source selection
  • Original identifiers and text

What happens next?

  • A structured draft note
  • Open questions and requests
  • MSL review and follow-up
Value hypothesis: less reconstruction effort and fewer missed commitments. Time savings and usefulness have not yet been measured.
notes: Present the benefit as a hypothesis. The application supports preparation and documentation; the MSL retains scientific judgment and responsibility for follow-up.

title: A complete local workflow, with clear boundaries
lead: Three workspaces connect the CRM snapshot to public evidence and reviewable drafts.
body:
3KOL profiles
9interactions
9tasks
6medical requests

01 | KOL context

Profile, interaction history, follow-up tasks and medical requests.

02 | Evidence search

PubMed and ClinicalTrials.gov filters, summaries and source selection.

03 | Drafts & follow-up

Priorities, briefing, note drafts and downloadable preparation records.

CRM snapshot: 23 October 2026. Read-only fixture data; no live CRM connection or task write-back.
notes: Explain the fixed dataset counts and snapshot date. Completed tasks are recorded fixture history, not actions performed by this application. Source retrieval uses public APIs.

title: Know the KOL before reviewing the evidence
lead: A profile organized around assignment, engagement preferences, scientific interests and the planned meeting.
body:
[[image:crm_profile_desktop.png|CRM profile: side-by-side record, engagement and meeting cards]]
Exact-ID retrievalSeparate KOL recordsWorkspace clears on KOL change
notes: Show Dr Mira Sen. Point out territory, preferred channel, scientific interests and planned meeting. Changing KOL clears notes, source selections, search results and prior drafts.

title: Keep the next action and the open question visible
lead: Read-only cards make status, ownership, dates and medical-information requests easier to scan.
body:
[[image:aligned_tasks_desktop.png|Follow-up tasks: status, owner, due date and closure evidence]]
[[image:aligned_requests_desktop.png|Medical requests: question, response status, source pack and linked task]]
Overdue uses the CRM snapshot date. Newly drafted requests do not assign an owner, set a deadline or change CRM status.
notes: Distinguish fixture ownership from generated follow-up. Full registers remain under expanders. New requests are drafts requiring review and assignment outside this application.

title: Filter the right source, using the right meaning
lead: Filters are sent to the public API before the returned-record limit is applied.
body:
[[image:aligned_pubmed_filters_desktop.png|PubMed publication, evidence, focus and access filters]]

PubMed: publication dates, article types, languages, availability, species, therapy keywords, affiliation and journal.

[[image:aligned_trials_filters_desktop.png|ClinicalTrials.gov treatment, recruitment, design, eligibility and date filters]]

Trials: treatment, location, recruitment, phase, design, eligibility and registry dates.

Author affiliation is not study location. Trial registration/update dates are not publication dates. Up to five returned records per search is not an exhaustive export.
notes: Explain source-specific meanings. PubMed therapy keywords search title/abstract. Trials provide intervention fields. Changing controls clears stale evidence without automatically searching.

title: A short overview, with the original evidence available
lead: Summaries support scanning. The briefing uses the original explicitly selected records.
body:
[[image:aligned_pubmed_results_desktop.png|Actual public-search snapshot: Offline excerpt, not an AI-generated summary]]

What the user reviews

  • PMID or NCT ID and original link
  • Offline excerpt / overview, or an explicit OpenAI summary request
  • Original abstract or registry details under an expander
  • Explicit source selection before preparation
PubMed retrieval is metadata/abstract based. Planned trial outcomes are not represented as study results.
notes: The screenshot is a real search snapshot in Offline mode. Do not call its excerpt an AI summary. OpenAI mode adds one public-record summary batch per successful nonempty search; CRM and notes are excluded from that request.

title: One responsibility per agent
lead: Exactly three application agents, coordinated by LangGraph.
body:
01KOL Context Agent

INPUT

Selected KOL ID and CRM history.

OUTPUT

Exact context; OpenAI mode adds meeting priorities and unresolved requests.

CRM is context, not scientific evidence.

02Scientific Source Agent

INPUT

Explicit searches and selected scientific sources.

OUTPUT

Retrieved records, summaries and a source-linked briefing with questions and limitations.

Missing sources trigger abstention.

03Follow-up Agent

INPUT

MSL-entered meeting notes.

OUTPUT

Preserved notes plus draft observations, requests and open questions.

New owners and dates remain unassigned.
notes: These are bounded roles, not three independent autonomous chatbots. The Scientific Source Agent owns explicit retrieval, search summaries and the scientific preparation node; retrieval is not a fourth agent.

title: A deterministic flow around bounded model calls
lead: The user chooses the KOL, initiates searches, selects evidence and explicitly requests preparation.
body:
Search time

Read-only public registry retrieval. In OpenAI mode, one public-record summary batch per nonempty search.

Preparation time

Offline or OpenAI drafting. Maximum three model requests; absent sources or notes can skip individual requests.
notes: Trace the graph from left to right. Identity resolves before model requests. Each role receives its own payload. Arrows show control order: the scientific model receives selected sources, not CRM context. Search-time requests are separate explicit actions.

title: Designed to make unsupported output visible
lead: Controls help the software fail clearly; they do not establish medical correctness.
body:
Before and during generation

  • Exact-ID lookup and input-size limits
  • Strict structured outputs and schema validation
  • Selected-source IDs and exact quote checks
  • Bounded output, timeout and sanitized errors

At the review boundary

  • Abstain without scientific evidence
  • Clear stale drafts after failure or changed criteria
  • Preserve original notes and scientific sources
  • Leave approval and external action with people
Matching a quote does not prove correct interpretation. No live CRM writes, external messages or safety submissions are implemented.
notes: Do not present controls as clinical validation or compliance certification. They constrain format, source references and quote occurrence. Human review must still assess scientific support, omissions and usefulness.

title: Software behavior tested, with separate evidence types
body:
{{TESTS}}automated test cases passed
{{HARNESS}}fixed harness cases passed
{{BROWSER}}desktop/mobile checks passed

Automated coverage

  • Agent contracts and graph order
  • KOL isolation and UI recovery
  • API parsing, filters and source selection
  • Schema, citation and quote rejection

Observed browser checks

  • Task and request card alignment
  • Live PubMed and trial retrieval
  • Grouped filters and visible summaries
  • Mobile layouts without page overflow
Harness cases overlap with unit-test behavior. These totals are not independent samples of model quality or a clinical-accuracy score.
notes: Open the evidence copies if challenged. Pytest cases use mocked services; browser checks include actual public retrieval and no model calls. Do not sum the counts into a single quality sample. The live OpenAI evaluation remains separate.

title: A repeatable experiment around the actual agents
lead: Local fake transport exercises production orchestration and parsing without API keys or network access.
body:
01Fixed cases

Synthetic inputs and explicit expected outcomes

02Scripted transport

Structured local responses and error cases

03Production graph

The same three agents and schema validation

04Named checks

Identity, role inputs, evidence and call budget

05Saved reports

JSON, readable results, versions and input hashes

Deliberate failure cases

Unknown identity, oversized input, missing evidence, unselected citations, invented quotes, refusals and malformed output.

Test the grader, too

Corrupt identity, notes, sources, credentials, role inputs, call order and other-KOL context; the grader must reject them.
notes: Distinguish runtime controls from evaluation. LangGraph and validation surround runtime requests. The evaluation harness supplies scripted responses and grades mechanical behavior. Network guards prevent accidental service calls. There is no model judge or live prompt-injection robustness claim.

title: Behavior contracts, implementation and evidence are separated
lead: The repository is also the Obsidian vault, keeping the supporting documentation together.
body:

notes: Explain the loop: define behavior, implement focused changes, map requirements to tests, run QA, then inspect evidence. Specifications exist; evaluator agreement on scope and thresholds is still pending.

title: A reliable path through the working application
lead: Start in Offline mode. Use OpenAI mode only for a separately configured and honestly labeled live run.
body:
1. Context | 1 minuteSelect Dr Mira Sen. Show the profile, prior history, open task and medical request.
  2. Evidence | 2 minutesRun public searches. Inspect a summary and original details; explicitly select a record.
  3. Drafts | 1 minuteEnter synthetic meeting notes and prepare. Explain Offline versus OpenAI behavior.
  4. Boundaries | 1 minuteShow abstention without selected evidence and workspace clearing on KOL change.
  5. Evidence | 1 minuteShow saved QA artifacts and identify remaining evaluator review.
Use the screenshot walkthroughOpen local app
notes: Have the app running first. Enter a key only in its password field, never on a slide. Offline mode preserves sources and formats notes; it does not interpret clinical evidence. The screenshot walkthrough is a fallback, not live model output.

title: The next milestone is reviewed evidence of usefulness
lead: The local build is ready to demonstrate. Model quality and stakeholder acceptance need their own evidence.
body:
Validate the outputs

  • Record a local OpenAI walkthrough
  • Check paraphrases against original sources
  • Exercise missing/conflicting evidence and hostile source text

Complete evaluator review

  • Name the reviewer and record decisions
  • Score E1-E8 with the prepared rubric
  • Measure a baseline before claiming time savings

Decide the next scope

  • Agree approval and task-tracking needs
  • Assess production identity and durable records
  • Confirm a permitted host with the team
Hosting remains on hold. No external public app URL has been created. The shareable HTML walkthrough works independently of hosting.
notes: Ask for a reviewer, date and acceptance decision. Functionality was explored, but no saved and reviewed live OpenAI report exists in the project evidence. No productivity or scientific-quality improvement has been measured.
